title: Neonatal bilious emesis + Ladd bands: failed midgut rotation and fixation (malrotation)
vignette: A 3-day-old boy is brought to the emergency department due to poor feeding, emesis, and lethargy over the past 24 hours. He was born via uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery to a 30-year-old woman who had a normal pregnancy. The boy was discharged from the newborn nursery yesterday and was breastfeeding exclusively until the onset of symptoms. Stool and urine output were normal while he was in the hospital. The patient is afebrile and normotensive but tachycardic and tachypneic. He appears dehydrated, and the abdomen is distended. The patient vomits during the examination; the vomitus is bilious (green). On laparotomy, fibrous bands are seen extending from the cecum and right colon to the retroperitoneum, causing extrinsic compression of the duodenum. Which of the following embryologic processes most likely failed in this patient?

clues.note: Bilious emesis in a neonate is a surgical emergency; malrotation with midgut volvulus and duodenal obstruction is the key concern.
Bilious (green) emesis indicates obstruction DISTAL to the ampulla of Vater (second part of duodenum) - here from Ladd bands compressing the duodenum.

clues.text: fibrous bands are seen extending from the cecum and right colon to the retroperitoneum, causing extrinsic compression of the duodenum
clues.note: These are LADD BANDS - the hallmark of intestinal MALROTATION, arising because the cecum failed to migrate to the right lower quadrant and instead fixes over the duodenum.

whatMatters: Bilious emesis in a neonate with LADD BANDS compressing the duodenum = intestinal MALROTATION, caused by FAILED midgut rotation and fixation. The cecum stays in the right upper quadrant and abnormal peritoneal bands cross and obstruct the duodenum (with risk of midgut volvulus). Answer B.
strategy: Bilious emesis + Ladd bands over the duodenum = malrotation from incomplete midgut rotation/fixation. Reject the other embryologic failures by their signatures: ventral/dorsal pancreatic bud fusion failure -> pancreas divisum (usually asymptomatic) or annular pancreas; neural crest migration failure -> Hirschsprung (delayed meconium, no Ladd bands); omphalomesenteric duct failure -> Meckel diverticulum (painless GI bleed); recanalization failure -> duodenal atresia (double bubble, no Ladd bands).

options.text: Fusion of the ventral and dorsal pancreatic buds
Neural crest cell migration into the bowel wall

eliminations.label: Pancreatic bud fusion failure - pancreas divisum
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: failure of ventral and dorsal pancreatic bud fusion -> pancreas divisum (or annular pancreas). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pancreas divisum is usually asymptomatic/incidental and does not create Ladd bands. ✅ Correct if: incidental dorsal-duct-dominant drainage or an annular pancreas encircling the duodenum.

eliminations.label: Neural crest migration failure - Hirschsprung
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: failed neural crest migration -> aganglionic colon (Hirschsprung disease). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes DELAYED meconium passage and a narrow aganglionic segment, not Ladd bands compressing the duodenum. ✅ Correct if: failure to pass meconium >48 h, distension relieved on rectal exam.

eliminations.label: Omphalomesenteric duct failure - Meckel diverticulum
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: failed obliteration of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct -> Meckel diverticulum. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Meckel typically presents with PAINLESS lower GI bleeding, not neonatal bilious emesis with Ladd bands. ✅ Correct if: painless hematochezia, ectopic gastric mucosa (rule of 2s).

eliminations.label: Recanalization failure - duodenal atresia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: failed recanalization of the duodenal lumen -> duodenal atresia (double-bubble sign, associated with Down syndrome). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: atresia causes obstruction WITHOUT Ladd bands; the operative finding here is fibrous bands from malrotation. ✅ Correct if: double bubble on x-ray, bilious emesis without Ladd bands.

reasoning: A neonate with bilious emesis and abdominal distension = obstruction distal to the ampulla of Vater
At laparotomy, Ladd bands cross from the malpositioned cecum/right colon to compress the duodenum
Ladd bands are the hallmark of intestinal malrotation
-> failed midgut rotation and fixation; answer B
mechanism: During weeks 4-8 of gestation the MIDGUT (supplied by the superior mesenteric artery) herniates through the umbilical ring, rotates 90 degrees counterclockwise, then returns to the abdomen and rotates an additional 180 degrees (270 degrees total counterclockwise), finally FIXING to the posterior abdominal wall on a broad-based mesentery (duodenojejunal flexure in the left upper quadrant, cecum in the right lower quadrant). INCOMPLETE rotation and fixation leaves the cecum in the right upper quadrant, and fibrous LADD BANDS extend from the malpositioned cecum/right colon across to the retroperitoneum, passing over and COMPRESSING the second part of the duodenum. This produces neonatal duodenal obstruction with BILIOUS EMESIS and distension. Malrotation also leaves a narrow mesenteric base prone to twisting around the SMA (midgut VOLVULUS), which can compromise perfusion and cause bowel ischemia/necrosis - a surgical emergency. The distractors correspond to distinct embryologic errors (pancreas divisum/annular pancreas, Hirschsprung, Meckel diverticulum, duodenal atresia) that lack Ladd bands.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Embryo/GI > intestinal malrotation: incomplete 270-degree counterclockwise midgut rotation/fixation; Ladd bands compress the duodenum; risk of midgut volvulus (twist around SMA); neonatal bilious emesis.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Ladd bands over the duodenum + bilious emesis = failed midgut rotation/fixation.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on midgut rotation, Ladd bands, malrotation, volvulus, ampulla of Vater, or bilious emesis? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Pancreatic bud fusion = divisum/annular; neural crest = Hirschsprung; vitelline duct = Meckel; recanalization = duodenal atresia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: neonatal bilious emesis + Ladd bands = malrotation; watch for midgut volvulus (SMA twist).
